subject.title: feat(compaction): add identifier survival validation after summarization

question: Should strict identifier-survival mode cancel compaction when recovery would exceed the summary cap, rather than return the capped summary with known identifier loss?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility and session-continuity policy choice, not a mechanical correctness question: either outcome can be defensible, but existing users may experience a different runtime failure mode.

options.title: Accept strict cancellation
options.body: Keep the proposed fail-closed behavior after end-to-end proof confirms that callers surface cancellation safely and do not silently continue with incomplete context.

options.title: Retry or warn without cancellation
options.body: Preserve existing compaction availability and record identifier loss, accepting that strict mode cannot guarantee identifier survival at the hard size cap.

options.title: Pause for narrower policy design
options.body: Defer the strict overflow behavior until maintainers define the desired user recovery path and compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Accept strict cancellation
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed fail-closed behavior after end-to-end proof confirms that callers surface cancellation safely and do not silently continue with incomplete context.
